Per session contract, a new sweep was seeded with bug-73. Prior state preserved in git history.

bugs.title: Super Series never actually activates in production - buildStageARequest (bot/src/github.js) silently STRIPPED series.super_series when persisting stage-a-request.json
bugs.notes: OPERATOR RE-REPORT (screenshots, 2026-09-12 ~23:02 +0100): a task created AFTER the prior sweep's 'done' still generated the ordinary single-part Series Mode prompt and rejected a whole-series plan with legacy flat-field errors (series_part/series_summary etc.). The prior sweep's conclusion 'handlers exist, it is a deployment lag' was WRONG in the decisive respect and this session corrected it with repo evidence. EVIDENCE: (1) git history shows the operator's toggle DID work in production - commit 4c8851d wrote branding/super_series_settings.json enabled:true at epoch 1789252763 (22:39:23 UTC), proving set:superseries:on was live on the deployed worker; (2) 4s later job manual-1789252767695 was created (22:39:27) and its FIRST persisted stage-a-request.json (commit 78cfd1d, 22:39:45) ALREADY lacked series.super_series entirely - at a moment the deployed code demonstrably had the toggle handler. ROOT CAUSE (verified against live code, not re-derived from the seeded hypothesis): wizardToRequest() (wizard.js:179) correctly emits series.super_series, and startJob (index.js:695) correctly sets wizard.superSeries from the setting - but buildStageARequest() in bot/src/github.js, the ONLY writer of jobs/<id>/stage-a-request.json, rebuilds the series object from an explicit allowlist {enabled, series_id, source_job_id, part, start_seconds, context} and DROPPED super_series. Every downstream consumer (handlePlanUploadMessage router at index.js:1341, bundle.py:121 prompt dispatch) reads the PERSISTED file, so the flag never reached any of them: the router always fell through to the ordinary single-part validator (producing exactly the legacy flat-field errors the operator saw) and bundle.py never fired the Super Series template (producing exactly the ordinary prompt the operator saw). Why the prior sweep missed it: its new tests asserted wizardToRequest's IN-MEMORY output and mocked/inspected handlers, but nothing asserted the flag survived the single disk boundary - the same class of gap as the original handler bug, one layer deeper. FIX (surgical, 3 files): (a) bot/src/github.js buildStageARequest now emits super_series:true into the persisted series block iff series.super_series===true (omitted otherwise so the router's ===true check and old readers are unaffected); (b) schemas/stage_a_request.schema.json gains optional series.super_series (additionalProperties:false made this mandatory); (c) NEW bot/test/super-series-persist.test.mjs (6 tests) pins the end-to-end chain wizard->wizardToRequest ->buildStageARequest->persisted doc: flag present and true for super jobs, key ABSENT for ordinary series jobs, force-dropped when series is off even with a stale superSeries:true token, and absent for series-less requests. CONTINUATIONS: spawned parts intentionally do NOT inherit super_series (they are per-part executors; series.js nextPartRequestBody correctly leaves it unset) - verified against super_series.js superPartRequestBody design. VERIFICATION: full bot suite 248/248 pass (242 prior + 6 new); pipeline super-series suite 15/15 pass; updated schema validated - the existing on-disk request for manual-1789252767695 still validates (key optional). Prior bug-73 handler tests (7) and feature-01 suites (14+15) all still green. OPERATOR NOTE: the fix is in the repo; the deployed bot worker must be redeployed from current main to write super_series:true for NEW tasks (existing in-flight jobs' requests on disk were already written without the flag and cannot be retro-routed).

sweep_summary: bug-73 REOPENED by operator screenshots and actually fixed this round: prior sweep blamed deployment lag, but git evidence (setting commit 4c8851d at 22:39:23, first request save 78cfd1d at 22:39:45 already lacking super_series) proved the toggle was live and the real defect was buildStageARequest stripping series.super_series at the single stage-a-request.json write boundary. Fixed in github.js + schema + 6 new end-to-end persistence tests; bot 248/248, pipeline super-series 15/15 green. No further pending bugs in this sweep.
